children: Lender sees rising demand for financing as India expands data centre capacity for artificial intelligence infrastructure

The National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (Nabfid) has sanctioned loans of more than Rs 3,000 crore each to at least four data centre projects as demand for artificial intelligence infrastructure grows in India.
The facilities have a moratorium of up to five years, followed by a repayment period of 10 years, Nabfid Managing Director Rajkiran Rai G. said in an interview.
Rai said such projects can generate “good” cash flows despite their long construction periods. Nabfid has also seen demand from hyperscalers, or large cloud service providers, he said.

The financing demand comes as companies increase spending on large data centre projects in India. Global investors including EQT AB, Blackstone and Alphabet, along with Indian conglomerates such as the Adani Group, have committed investments towards data centre and artificial intelligence infrastructure in the country.
Nabfid estimates that India's data centre sector will require about Rs 1 trillion in funding through March 2031, according to a presentation by the lender.
Nabfid is looking to diversify its borrowing sources and has prepared to raise funds through its maiden dollar bond.
The lender plans to raise Rs 1 trillion during the year ending March 2027, with about 40 per cent of the amount expected to come from overseas sources by the end of December, Rai said.

Nabfid has raised close to USD 1 billion through offshore loans under a concessional window provided by the Reserve Bank of India and available until 31 December. It has also mandated foreign banks to mobilise a 10-year dollar bond of a similar amount through the window by the end of September, Rai said.
